items.title: Select the 3 findings that suggest worsening oxygenation in an adult with pneumonia.
items.content: New confusion; central cyanosis; increasing work of breathing with falling saturation.
items.rationale: Altered mentation, cyanosis, and increased respiratory effort with hypoxemia indicate deterioration.

items.title: Match each infection with the primary transmission-based precaution.
items.content: rows:measles;influenza;MRSA wound with uncontrolled drainage|columns:airborne;droplet;contact|answers:measles=airborne;influenza=droplet;MRSA wound with uncontrolled drainage=contact
items.rationale: Measles requires airborne precautions, influenza droplet precautions, and uncontrolled draining MRSA wounds contact precautions.

items.title: A client receiving unfractionated heparin develops serious bleeding. The nurse should stop the infusion and anticipate prescribed ___ as a reversal agent while monitoring ___ and hemodynamic status.
items.content: protamine sulfate|aPTT
items.rationale: Protamine reverses unfractionated heparin. Monitor coagulation parameters and clinical bleeding response.

items.title: A client with heart failure suddenly becomes severely dyspneic, has crackles, pink frothy sputum, and SpO₂ 80%. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute pulmonary edema|actions:activate emergency response and support oxygenation;position upright and prepare prescribed ventilatory and diuretic therapy|monitor:oxygen saturation and respiratory effort;blood pressure and urine output
items.rationale: Severe pulmonary congestion with hypoxemia is life-threatening. Escalate, support ventilation, position upright, and prepare prescribed therapy while monitoring response.

items.title: Highlight the actions that reduce aspiration risk after stroke: complete swallow screening before oral intake; offer thin water before assessment; position upright for meals; check for food pocketing; keep suction available when indicated.
items.content: segments:complete swallow screening before oral intake|offer thin water before assessment|position upright for meals|check for food pocketing|keep suction available when indicated|correct:1,3,4,5
items.rationale: Swallow screening before intake, upright positioning, checking for pocketing, and appropriate suction readiness reduce aspiration harm.

items.title: A client’s weight increases from 68.2 kg to 70.0 kg. What is the weight gain in kg?
items.rationale: 70.0 − 68.2 = 1.8 kg. Rapid weight gain may reflect fluid retention and should be interpreted with the care plan.

items.title: A client taking lithium has a level of 0.8 mEq/L last week and 1.7 mEq/L today with vomiting and coarse tremor. What is the priority?
items.content: Suspect lithium toxicity; withhold further doses pending urgent prescriber direction and obtain clinical assessment.
items.rationale: A rising level above the usual therapeutic range with toxicity symptoms requires urgent evaluation, hydration assessment, and renal/electrolyte review.

items.title: A client with a high spinal cord injury develops hypotension, bradycardia, and warm dry skin. Which complication should the nurse suspect?
items.content: Neurogenic shock.
items.rationale: Loss of sympathetic tone can cause hypotension, bradycardia, and vasodilation after spinal cord injury.

items.title: A client with pancreatic cancer has jaundice, pruritus, and pale stools. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Assess skin integrity; monitor bilirubin and liver tests; provide prescribed antipruritic care; assess nutritional status and stool changes.
items.rationale: Biliary obstruction can cause cholestasis, pruritus, pale stools, and malabsorption. Monitor hepatic function, skin, and nutrition.

items.title: Select the 3 actions appropriate for recurrent late decelerations during oxytocin infusion.
items.content: Stop oxytocin; reposition the client laterally; notify the obstetric clinician promptly.
items.rationale: These actions reduce uterine stimulation, may improve perfusion, and escalate evaluation of fetal compromise.

items.title: For each abnormality, select the appropriate safety focus.
items.content: rows:potassium 2.8 mEq/L;magnesium 1.1 mg/dL;sodium 119 mEq/L|columns:monitor cardiac rhythm;assess neuromuscular irritability;monitor neurologic status and correction rate|answers:potassium 2.8 mEq/L=monitor cardiac rhythm;magnesium 1.1 mg/dL=assess neuromuscular irritability,monitor cardiac rhythm;sodium 119 mEq/L=monitor neurologic status and correction rate
items.rationale: Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia can cause dysrhythmias. Hypomagnesemia also causes neuromuscular irritability. Severe hyponatremia requires neurologic monitoring and careful correction.

items.title: An 8-year-old with asthma has severe wheezing, speaks in one-word phrases, RR 36/min, and SpO₂ 89%. After initial bronchodilator, breath sounds become very faint and the child is drowsy. What is the priority?
items.content: Recognize impending respiratory failure, activate emergency airway support, provide oxygen and prescribed rescue therapy, and prepare for ventilatory support.
items.rationale: A quiet chest with drowsiness after severe distress suggests critically reduced airflow and fatigue, not improvement. Immediate escalation is essential.

items.title: A client experiencing paranoid delusions refuses food because they believe it is poisoned. Which response is most therapeutic?
items.content: Offer sealed, unopened food and acknowledge the client's fear without reinforcing the delusion.
items.rationale: A practical choice can support nutrition and trust. Validate emotion without agreeing with the delusional belief.

items.title: Which interventions may reduce delirium in an older hospitalized client? Select all that apply.
items.content: Provide orientation cues; promote sleep hygiene; ensure sensory aids are available; encourage mobility and hydration; minimize unnecessary room changes.
items.rationale: Orientation, sleep, sensory support, mobility, and hydration reduce delirium risk. Investigate acute causes such as infection, medication effects, and hypoxia.

items.title: Select the 3 immediate nursing priorities for suspected compartment syndrome.
items.content: Notify the surgical team urgently; perform and document neurovascular assessments; prepare for pressure-relieving intervention as prescribed.
items.rationale: Compartment syndrome threatens limb viability. Urgent surgical evaluation and serial neurovascular assessment are essential.

items.title: Match each insulin with its general action profile.
items.content: rows:lispro;regular;glargine|columns:rapid acting;short acting;long acting basal|answers:lispro=rapid acting;regular=short acting;glargine=long acting basal
items.rationale: Lispro is rapid acting, regular insulin is short acting, and glargine provides long-acting basal coverage. Timing must follow product guidance and meal availability.

items.title: A client with aortic stenosis reports exertional syncope and chest pain. These symptoms suggest reduced ___ output. The nurse should avoid unmonitored strenuous ___ and report symptoms promptly to the ___.
items.content: cardiac|activity|cardiology team
items.rationale: Aortic stenosis obstructs left ventricular outflow. Syncope and angina suggest limited cardiac output and require prompt specialist assessment.

items.title: A client with diabetes is unconscious, glucose 32 mg/dL, and has no IV access. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:severe hypoglycemia|actions:administer prescribed glucagon by an available approved route;activate emergency response and establish IV access for dextrose if needed|monitor:repeat blood glucose;level of consciousness and ability to swallow safely
items.rationale: Unconscious hypoglycemia is an emergency. Give glucagon if IV access is unavailable, obtain emergency support, and reassess glucose and neurologic status.

items.title: Highlight findings indicating worsening fluid overload: increasing orthopnea; new crackles; rapid weight gain; reduced peripheral edema; rising jugular venous pressure.
items.content: segments:increasing orthopnea|new crackles|rapid weight gain|reduced peripheral edema|rising jugular venous pressure|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Orthopnea, crackles, rapid weight gain, and elevated JVP indicate worsening congestion. Reduced edema alone does not suggest fluid overload.

items.title: A client is prescribed 0.5 mg of a medication. Tablets are 0.25 mg each. How many tablets should be given?
items.content: 2|tablets|0
items.rationale: 0.5 mg ÷ 0.25 mg/tablet = 2 tablets. Verify the prescribed dose and tablet formulation.

items.title: A client with suspected shock has MAP readings of 62, 58, and 54 mm Hg with decreasing urine output. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: Perfusion is worsening and requires immediate escalation and prescribed hemodynamic support.
items.rationale: A falling MAP with oliguria indicates worsening organ perfusion. Prompt escalation and reassessment are necessary.

items.title: A 76-year-old admitted with ischemic stroke has facial weakness and slurred speech. During a bedside water trial, the client coughs and develops a wet voice. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Stop the oral trial, maintain NPO status, notify the clinician, and request formal swallowing evaluation. Continue aspiration precautions and provide oral care.
items.rationale: Coughing and wet voice indicate possible aspiration. Oral intake should stop pending formal swallowing assessment; oral hygiene reduces aspiration pneumonia risk.

items.title: Immediately after placental delivery, a client has severe hemorrhage, shock, and a mass protruding from the vagina; the uterine fundus is not palpable abdominally. What should the nurse suspect?
items.content: Uterine inversion and activate the obstetric emergency response.
items.rationale: A missing abdominal fundus with a vaginal mass and hemorrhage suggests uterine inversion, a life-threatening obstetric emergency.

items.title: Which interventions are appropriate for a client with increased intracranial pressure? Select all that apply.
items.content: Elevate the head of bed as prescribed; keep head and neck midline; avoid unnecessary stimulation; prevent hypoxia and hypotension; cluster all care into prolonged sessions.
items.rationale: Positioning and prevention of hypoxia/hypotension support cerebral perfusion. Avoid excessive stimulation and prolonged clustering that can increase ICP.

items.title: Select the 3 priority elements of medication reconciliation at admission.
items.content: Compare the client's actual medication use with the current orders; verify allergies and prior adverse reactions; identify duplicate therapies and high-risk interactions.
items.rationale: Accurate reconciliation requires a best possible medication history, allergy review, and identification of discrepancies, duplication, and interactions.

items.title: Match each clinical pattern with the likely shock category.
items.content: rows:severe dehydration with tachycardia and flat neck veins;sepsis with warm flushed skin early and hypotension;massive MI with pulmonary crackles and hypotension|columns:hypovolemic;distributive;cardiogenic|answers:severe dehydration with tachycardia and flat neck veins=hypovolemic;sepsis with warm flushed skin early and hypotension=distributive;massive MI with pulmonary crackles and hypotension=cardiogenic
items.rationale: Volume loss causes hypovolemic shock; sepsis causes distributive shock; pump failure with pulmonary congestion suggests cardiogenic shock.

items.title: A client with unilateral calf swelling and pain after surgery may have a ___. The nurse should avoid massaging the limb and anticipate diagnostic ___ as prescribed.
items.content: deep vein thrombosis|ultrasound
items.rationale: Unilateral swelling and pain suggest DVT. Massage is avoided; duplex ultrasound is commonly used for diagnosis.

items.title: A client with Graves disease has fever 40.2 °C, HR 160/min, agitation, and diarrhea. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:thyroid storm|actions:activate urgent medical response and initiate cooling measures;administer prescribed beta blocker and antithyroid therapy|monitor:heart rate and rhythm;temperature and mental status
items.rationale: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening hypermetabolic emergency. Cooling, beta blockade, and antithyroid therapy are used with close cardiovascular and neurologic monitoring.

items.title: Highlight findings of severe dehydration in an infant: lethargy; markedly delayed capillary refill; absent tears; normal wet diapers; weak peripheral pulses.
items.content: segments:lethargy|markedly delayed capillary refill|absent tears|normal wet diapers|weak peripheral pulses|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Lethargy, delayed refill, absent tears, and weak pulses indicate significant volume depletion and impaired perfusion.

items.title: A 70-kg adult produces 21 mL of urine in 1 hour. Calculate urine output in mL/kg/hr to two decimal places.
items.rationale: 21 mL ÷ 70 kg = 0.30 mL/kg/hr, below the usual adult target of at least 0.5 mL/kg/hr.

items.title: A chemotherapy client's temperature rises from 37.2 °C to 38.1 °C and ANC is 400/mm³. What is the priority?
items.content: Treat as febrile neutropenia and activate urgent evaluation and antimicrobial pathway.
items.rationale: Fever with severe neutropenia is an emergency even without localizing symptoms; prompt empiric antimicrobial treatment is required.

items.title: A 63-year-old on postoperative day 2 develops sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, HR 132/min, BP 94/58 mm Hg, and SpO₂ 85%. One calf is swollen. What is the priority nursing plan?
items.content: Suspect pulmonary embolism with possible hemodynamic compromise. Activate rapid response, support oxygenation, keep the client at rest, establish monitoring and IV access, and prepare for urgent imaging and prescribed anticoagulation or advanced therapy.
items.rationale: Sudden respiratory symptoms, hypoxemia, tachycardia, hypotension, and unilateral leg swelling suggest PE. Immediate stabilization and urgent evaluation are necessary.

items.title: A competent adult client refuses a prescribed medication after receiving an explanation. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Respect the refusal, assess the reason, provide relevant information, and notify the prescriber as appropriate.
items.rationale: Competent adults may refuse treatment. The nurse should explore concerns, educate without coercion, document, and communicate the decision.

items.title: Which findings should a client with a new ileostomy report promptly? Select all that apply.
items.content: Stoma becomes dusky or black; persistent absence of output with cramping and vomiting; signs of dehydration; markedly increased watery output.
items.rationale: Dusky/black stoma may indicate ischemia. Obstruction and high-output ileostomy can cause dehydration and electrolyte loss.

items.title: Select the 3 postpartum symptoms that require urgent evaluation.
items.content: Heavy bleeding soaking a pad in an hour or less; severe headache with visual changes; chest pain or difficulty breathing.
items.rationale: These may indicate hemorrhage, postpartum preeclampsia, pulmonary embolism, or cardiac complications and require urgent care.

items.title: For each specimen, select the appropriate collection principle.
items.content: rows:clean-catch urine;blood culture;stool for occult blood|columns:cleanse and collect midstream;use aseptic venipuncture and collect before antibiotics when feasible;avoid contamination with urine or toilet water|answers:clean-catch urine=cleanse and collect midstream;blood culture=use aseptic venipuncture and collect before antibiotics when feasible;stool for occult blood=avoid contamination with urine or toilet water
items.rationale: Correct collection reduces contamination and false results. Blood cultures should be obtained before antibiotics when feasible without delaying urgent treatment.

items.title: Arrange the initial actions for a client with active hematemesis and hypotension.
items.content: Activate emergency response and assess airway, breathing, and circulation.|Position to protect airway and provide oxygen as indicated.|Establish large-bore IV access and initiate prescribed resuscitation.|Prepare for ordered blood products and urgent endoscopic evaluation.
items.rationale: Stabilization begins with ABCs and escalation, followed by IV access and resuscitation. Definitive evaluation follows stabilization.

items.title: Select all appropriate teaching points for a client with advanced chronic kidney disease.
items.content: Follow individualized sodium, potassium, phosphorus, and fluid guidance; attend scheduled renal appointments; report reduced urine output or new dyspnea; avoid OTC NSAIDs unless approved; use salt substitutes freely.
items.rationale: Diet and fluid limits must be individualized. NSAIDs can worsen renal function; many salt substitutes contain potassium and may be unsafe.

items.title: A client admitted for depression says, “I have saved enough medication to end my life when I get home.” The client has a prior attempt and refuses to discuss a safety plan. What is the priority?
items.content: Treat as high and potentially imminent suicide risk: maintain continuous observation per policy, secure medications and other means, notify the psychiatric team urgently, and complete direct risk assessment and safety planning.
items.rationale: A specific plan, access to means, prior attempt, and refusal of safety planning indicate high risk. Protect the client and escalate immediately; do not leave the client alone.

items.title: A client with a known severe food allergy develops throat tightness and wheezing after accidental exposure. Which action should the client take?
items.content: Use the epinephrine autoinjector immediately and activate emergency medical services.
items.rationale: Epinephrine is first-line for anaphylaxis. Antihistamines do not replace epinephrine or emergency evaluation.

items.title: A client with chronic hypercapnic COPD is prescribed controlled oxygen. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Use the prescribed delivery device and target saturation; reassess respiratory effort and mental status; obtain ABGs as ordered; titrate oxygen according to the prescribed plan.
items.rationale: Controlled oxygen reduces hypoxemia while avoiding unnecessary excess. Monitor clinical status and ABGs; never withhold oxygen from a hypoxemic client.

items.title: Select the 3 findings after myocardial infarction that require immediate escalation.
items.content: New hypotension; new pulmonary edema; sustained ventricular tachycardia.
items.rationale: These indicate cardiogenic shock, acute heart failure, or life-threatening dysrhythmia.

items.title: Match each medication with a serious adverse effect to report.
items.content: rows:ACE inhibitor;statin;amiodarone|columns:angioedema;unexplained muscle pain with dark urine;new dyspnea or cough|answers:ACE inhibitor=angioedema;statin=unexplained muscle pain with dark urine;amiodarone=new dyspnea or cough
items.rationale: ACE inhibitors can cause angioedema. Statins rarely cause rhabdomyolysis. Amiodarone can cause pulmonary toxicity.

items.title: A client with suspected STEMI should receive rapid ECG assessment and activation of the ___ pathway. The priority definitive treatment is timely ___ when indicated.
items.content: STEMI|reperfusion
items.rationale: STEMI requires rapid system activation and reperfusion, typically primary PCI when timely and appropriate.

items.title: A child sits leaning forward, drools, has a muffled voice, and inspiratory stridor. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute epiglottitis|actions:keep the child calm and avoid throat examination;activate expert airway support and prepare controlled airway management|monitor:work of breathing and oxygenation;level of consciousness
items.rationale: Epiglottitis can cause sudden airway obstruction. Avoid agitation and throat manipulation; secure expert airway support and monitor respiratory status.

items.title: Highlight findings in a client taking an antipsychotic that suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome: high fever;severe muscle rigidity;altered mental status;lead-pipe rigidity;isolated mild rhinorrhea.
items.content: segments:high fever|severe muscle rigidity|altered mental status|lead-pipe rigidity|isolated mild rhinorrhea|correct:1,2,3,4
items.rationale: Hyperthermia, severe rigidity, and mental-status change after dopamine-blocking medication suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a medical emergency.

items.title: A client's BP is 90/60 mm Hg. Calculate MAP using (SBP + 2 × DBP) ÷ 3. Enter a whole number.
items.content: 70|mm Hg|0

items.title: A postoperative client's temperature rises from 37.1 °C to 38.3 °C, HR from 88 to 116/min, and incision drainage becomes purulent. What is the priority?
items.content: Suspect surgical site infection with possible systemic involvement and notify the surgical team promptly.
items.rationale: Fever, tachycardia, and purulent drainage suggest infection requiring evaluation, cultures as ordered, and treatment.

items.title: A nurse discovers that a client received twice the prescribed dose of an antihypertensive 20 minutes ago. The client is currently asymptomatic. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Assess vital signs and symptoms immediately, notify the prescriber and appropriate safety personnel, follow orders for monitoring or treatment, and complete factual documentation and incident reporting per policy.
items.rationale: A medication error requires prompt assessment and disclosure through the appropriate clinical chain. Do not wait for symptoms or alter the record.

items.title: A client recovering from mild acute pancreatitis has improving pain and no vomiting. Which diet approach should the nurse anticipate?
items.content: Begin oral feeding as tolerated according to the prescribed plan, often with a low-fat approach.
items.rationale: Early oral feeding as tolerated is appropriate in many mild cases; prolonged routine NPO status is not necessary once symptoms permit intake.

items.title: Which findings suggest a client is ready for discharge after uncomplicated surgery? Select all that apply.
items.content: Stable vital signs; controlled pain with oral medication; tolerating oral fluids or diet as ordered; safe mobility at the expected level; unresolved new hypoxia.
items.rationale: Discharge requires stability and safe function. New hypoxia is a reason for further evaluation, not discharge.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that indicate worsening hepatic synthetic or neurologic function.
items.content: Rising INR; increasing confusion; recurrent hypoglycemia.
items.rationale: INR reflects impaired clotting factor synthesis; confusion suggests encephalopathy; hypoglycemia can occur with severe liver failure.

items.title: Match each wound drainage description with its term.
items.content: rows:clear watery drainage;pink-tinged thin drainage;thick yellow-green drainage|columns:serous;serosanguineous;purulent|answers:clear watery drainage=serous;pink-tinged thin drainage=serosanguineous;thick yellow-green drainage=purulent
items.rationale: Serous is clear, serosanguineous is pink-tinged, and purulent drainage is thick and may indicate infection.

items.title: Before thrombolytic therapy is considered for ischemic stroke, urgent brain imaging must exclude intracranial ___. The nurse must establish the last-known-___ time and check bedside ___.
items.content: hemorrhage|well|glucose
items.rationale: Imaging excludes hemorrhage, last-known-well time guides eligibility, and glucose identifies a common stroke mimic.

items.topic: Acute renal failure with fluid overload
items.title: A client with acute kidney injury has crackles, increasing edema, BP 182/100 mm Hg, and declining urine output. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute kidney injury with fluid overload|actions:notify the provider and prepare for prescribed fluid/diuretic or renal replacement plan;position to support breathing and restrict fluids only as prescribed|monitor:respiratory status and oxygenation;daily weight and intake/output
items.rationale: Oliguria with edema and crackles indicates fluid overload. Escalate, support breathing, and follow individualized fluid and renal treatment orders.

items.title: Highlight findings that suggest late neurovascular compromise: paralysis; pulselessness; pallor; severe pain; paresthesia.
items.content: segments:paralysis|pulselessness|pallor|severe pain|paresthesia|correct:1,2,3,4,5
items.rationale: All listed findings are concerning. Paralysis and pulselessness are late signs; intervention should occur before these develop.

items.title: A 500-mL IV bag is prescribed over 4 hours. What pump rate in mL/hr is required?
items.rationale: 500 mL ÷ 4 hr = 125 mL/hr.

items.title: A client with COPD has RR 28/min and SpO₂ 90% on prescribed oxygen. Later, RR falls to 10/min, the client becomes drowsy, and PaCO₂ rises. What does this trend indicate?
items.content: Worsening ventilatory failure and fatigue, requiring immediate escalation.
items.rationale: A falling respiratory rate with drowsiness and rising CO₂ may indicate fatigue rather than improvement.

items.title: A client at 36 weeks with preeclampsia has a generalized seizure. What are the immediate nursing priorities?
items.content: Call for help, protect the client from injury, position laterally when possible, support airway and oxygenation, administer prescribed magnesium sulfate, and prepare for maternal-fetal reassessment and delivery planning.
items.rationale: Eclampsia is an obstetric emergency. Stabilize airway and circulation, prevent injury, treat seizures with magnesium, and reassess mother and fetus.

items.title: A child with croup has stridor only when crying and no retractions at rest. Which intervention is most appropriate?
items.content: Keep the child calm and administer prescribed corticosteroid therapy.
items.rationale: Mild croup is managed with calm supportive care and corticosteroid treatment; agitation can worsen airway symptoms.

items.title: Which teaching points are appropriate for a client newly prescribed an oral anticoagulant for atrial fibrillation? Select all that apply.
items.content: Take the medication exactly as prescribed; report bleeding; inform clinicians before procedures; avoid starting OTC NSAIDs without advice.
items.rationale: Anticoagulation reduces embolic stroke risk but increases bleeding risk. Adherence and interaction awareness are essential.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that should trigger rapid response activation in a hospitalized adult.
items.content: Acute change in consciousness; severe respiratory distress; persistent hypotension with signs of poor perfusion.
items.rationale: These are indicators of potentially life-threatening deterioration requiring immediate escalation.

items.title: Match each breath sound with its common association.
items.content: rows:crackles;high-pitched wheeze;stridor|columns:fluid in alveoli or small airways;airflow through narrowed lower airways;upper airway obstruction|answers:crackles=fluid in alveoli or small airways;high-pitched wheeze=airflow through narrowed lower airways;stridor=upper airway obstruction
items.rationale: Crackles may reflect fluid or alveolar reopening, wheezes indicate narrowed lower airways, and stridor suggests upper airway obstruction.

items.title: A restraint may be used only after less restrictive measures fail and with an appropriate ___ and ongoing ___ according to policy. The client must be released as soon as it is ___ to do so.
items.content: order|monitoring|safe
items.rationale: Restraints require legal and policy-compliant authorization, ongoing reassessment, and prompt discontinuation when no longer necessary.

items.title: A septic client develops oozing from IV sites, petechiae, platelets 42,000/mm³, and prolonged PT/aPTT. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:disseminated intravascular coagulation|actions:notify the critical care team and treat the underlying sepsis;implement bleeding precautions and prepare prescribed blood component support|monitor:platelet count and coagulation studies;clinical bleeding and organ perfusion
items.rationale: DIC causes consumption of platelets and clotting factors with simultaneous bleeding and thrombosis. Treat the cause, support coagulation as prescribed, and monitor bleeding and perfusion.

items.title: Highlight findings of acute pulmonary edema: pink frothy sputum;severe dyspnea;bilateral crackles;orthopnea;dry cough without hypoxia or distress.
items.content: segments:pink frothy sputum|severe dyspnea|bilateral crackles|orthopnea|dry cough without hypoxia or distress|correct:1,2,3,4
items.rationale: Pink frothy sputum, severe dyspnea, crackles, and orthopnea are consistent with pulmonary edema.

items.title: A child weighs 20 kg. Using the 4-2-1 rule, calculate the hourly maintenance fluid rate in mL/hr.
items.content: 60|mL/hr|0
items.rationale: For the first 10 kg: 4 mL/kg/hr = 40; next 10 kg: 2 mL/kg/hr = 20; total 60 mL/hr. Clinical orders may use different methods and require reassessment.

items.title: A client with chest pain has troponin values that rise from 18 to 240 ng/L over 3 hours and develops new ST depression. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: Evolving myocardial injury with ongoing ischemia; escalate urgently for acute coronary syndrome management.
items.rationale: A rising troponin with ischemic ECG changes supports acute myocardial injury and requires urgent evaluation and treatment.

items.title: A 24-year-old with asthma has severe dyspnea, speaks in short phrases, RR 32/min, and SpO₂ 88%. After repeated rescue treatment, the client becomes drowsy and wheezing is no longer audible. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Activate emergency airway support immediately; provide oxygen and prescribed rescue therapy while preparing for ventilatory support.
items.rationale: Loss of wheezing with drowsiness in a severely distressed client may indicate minimal airflow and impending respiratory arrest, not recovery.

items.title: A client says they take an herbal supplement but cannot recall its name. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Ask the client to bring the container or obtain the exact product and dose before evaluating interactions.
items.rationale: Herbal products can interact with prescribed medications; identify the exact product, dose, and frequency rather than assuming its contents.

items.title: A client with a new ileostomy has output of 2.2 L/day and dizziness. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Assess vital signs and orthostatic symptoms; monitor electrolytes and renal function; notify the care team; follow prescribed oral rehydration and output management plan.
items.rationale: High ileostomy output can cause dehydration, electrolyte loss, and acute kidney injury. Prompt assessment and individualized replacement are needed.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that support suspected aortic dissection.
items.content: Abrupt tearing chest or back pain; unequal peripheral pulses or arm blood pressures; new neurologic deficit or syncope.
items.rationale: Abrupt tearing pain with pulse/BP differential or neurologic symptoms is concerning for dissection and requires emergency evaluation.

items.title: For each sick-day instruction, select whether it is appropriate.
items.content: rows:continue basal insulin unless specifically directed otherwise;check glucose more frequently;check ketones when indicated;stop all fluids during vomiting|columns:appropriate;inappropriate|answers:continue basal insulin unless specifically directed otherwise=appropriate;check glucose more frequently=appropriate;check ketones when indicated=appropriate;stop all fluids during vomiting=inappropriate
items.rationale: Sick-day plans generally continue basal insulin, increase glucose monitoring, check ketones when indicated, and maintain hydration with urgent care for red flags.

items.title: Arrange the immediate sequence for a client with suspected acute stroke.
items.content: Activate stroke response and record last-known-well time.|Assess ABCs and check bedside glucose.|Prepare for urgent noncontrast head CT.|Maintain NPO status until swallow screening is completed.
items.rationale: Rapid activation and time documentation are followed by stabilization and glucose assessment, imaging, and aspiration precautions.

items.title: Select all appropriate actions before administering a high-alert medication.
items.content: Verify the prescription and patient identity; check relevant laboratory results; use the required independent double-check per policy; program the infusion pump using the approved protocol; bypass barcode scanning if the unit is busy.
items.rationale: High-alert medications require verification, relevant monitoring, and policy-based safeguards. Workflow pressure is not a reason to bypass safety checks.

items.title: A client with a known neck mass develops stridor, drooling, and inability to speak full sentences. SpO₂ is 90%. What is the priority response?
items.content: Activate emergency airway support, keep the client upright and calm, provide oxygen as tolerated, and prepare for controlled airway management. Avoid unnecessary oral or throat manipulation.
items.rationale: Stridor and drooling suggest critical upper airway narrowing. Early expert airway management is safer than waiting for complete obstruction.

items.title: A newborn is wet immediately after birth. Which action best prevents heat loss?
items.content: Dry the newborn thoroughly and remove wet linens.
items.rationale: Evaporation from wet skin causes neonatal heat loss. Drying and replacing wet linens are immediate measures.

items.title: Which actions reduce medication errors in children? Select all that apply.
items.content: Use current weight in kilograms; calculate dose by weight and verify maximum dose; use an oral syringe for liquid medication; perform an independent check when required.
items.rationale: Pediatric dosing is weight-based and errors can be serious. Use kilograms, verify maximums, and measure liquids accurately.

items.title: A client in alcohol withdrawal has a generalized seizure. Select the 3 priority actions.
items.content: Protect the client from injury; maintain airway and position laterally when possible; administer prescribed benzodiazepine and activate urgent support.
items.rationale: Seizure safety, airway protection, and benzodiazepine treatment are priorities in alcohol withdrawal.

items.title: Match each presentation with the likely acute complication.
items.content: rows:deep rapid breathing, abdominal pain, ketones;profound dehydration, very high glucose, high osmolality;confusion and sweating with glucose 42 mg/dL|columns:diabetic ketoacidosis;hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state;hypoglycemia|answers:deep rapid breathing, abdominal pain, ketones=diabetic ketoacidosis;profound dehydration, very high glucose, high osmolality=hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state;confusion and sweating with glucose 42 mg/dL=hypoglycemia
items.rationale: DKA includes ketosis and metabolic acidosis. HHS features severe hyperglycemia and hyperosmolality. Low glucose with autonomic/neuroglycopenic symptoms indicates hypoglycemia.

items.title: For a client with suspected acute coronary syndrome, administer prescribed aspirin after checking for ___, and do not delay urgent ___ for routine tasks.
items.content: contraindications|reperfusion
items.rationale: Aspirin is commonly used unless contraindicated. Reperfusion is time-critical in STEMI and should not be delayed by routine activities.

items.title: A client with atrial fibrillation develops sudden severe leg pain, pallor, coolness, and absent distal pulse. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute limb ischemia from arterial occlusion|actions:notify vascular surgery/emergency team immediately;keep limb at neutral level and prepare for prescribed anticoagulation or revascularization|monitor:distal pulses and limb sensation/movement;skin temperature and color
items.rationale: Acute arterial occlusion threatens limb viability. Urgent vascular evaluation and serial neurovascular assessment are required; avoid massage or compression.

items.title: Highlight findings indicating impaired perfusion in a client with infection: altered mentation;oliguria;cool mottled extremities;normal capillary refill;MAP 55 mm Hg.
items.content: segments:altered mentation|oliguria|cool mottled extremities|normal capillary refill|MAP 55 mm Hg|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Altered mentation, oliguria, mottling, and low MAP indicate impaired perfusion and possible septic shock.

items.title: A 750-mL infusion is prescribed over 6 hours. Calculate the rate in mL/hr.
items.rationale: 750 mL ÷ 6 hours = 125 mL/hr.

items.title: A client receiving IV fluids develops increasing weight, crackles, rising BP, and decreasing oxygen saturation. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: The client may be developing fluid overload and pulmonary edema; stop or adjust fluids only according to protocol/order and escalate promptly.
items.rationale: The trend suggests worsening volume overload with respiratory compromise. Prompt assessment and prescriber notification are required.

items.title: A 70-year-old develops sudden severe headache, vomiting, and decreased consciousness. BP is 212/118 mm Hg. CT confirms intracerebral hemorrhage. What are the priority nursing concerns?
items.content: Maintain airway and oxygenation, perform frequent neurologic assessments, manage blood pressure using prescribed protocol, monitor for increased ICP, and avoid antithrombotic medications unless specifically directed.
items.rationale: Intracerebral hemorrhage can expand and cause increased ICP. Airway, neurologic monitoring, and controlled BP management are priorities.

items.title: A client with decision-making capacity refuses intubation and has a documented advance directive. The family demands intubation. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Advocate for the client's documented wishes and notify the care team.
items.rationale: A capable client's informed decisions and valid advance directive guide care; family disagreement does not override the client's wishes.

items.title: Which measures reduce aspiration pneumonia risk in a client with impaired swallowing? Select all that apply.
items.content: Follow swallow evaluation recommendations; provide upright positioning during meals; perform oral care; supervise feeding as indicated.
items.rationale: Swallow strategies, upright positioning, oral hygiene, and supervision reduce aspiration and bacterial burden.

items.title: Select the 3 findings most consistent with opioid toxicity.
items.content: Respiratory rate 6/min; pinpoint pupils; decreased level of consciousness.
items.rationale: Respiratory depression, miosis, and CNS depression are classic opioid toxicity findings.

items.title: Match each heart sound finding with its common interpretation.
items.content: rows:S3 in a client with dyspnea and edema;pericardial friction rub;new systolic murmur after MI|columns:possible volume overload/heart failure;pericardial inflammation;possible papillary muscle or septal complication|answers:S3 in a client with dyspnea and edema=possible volume overload/heart failure;pericardial friction rub=pericardial inflammation;new systolic murmur after MI=possible papillary muscle or septal complication
items.rationale: S3 with congestion suggests heart failure. A friction rub suggests pericardial inflammation. A new murmur after MI may signal a mechanical complication.

items.title: A client with severe respiratory distress who becomes drowsy and has a weak cough may be developing respiratory ___. The nurse should activate emergency support and prepare for airway ___.
items.content: failure|management
items.rationale: Drowsiness and weak cough in severe distress suggest fatigue and inability to protect the airway; urgent escalation is necessary.

items.title: A client receiving packed red cells develops urticaria, wheezing, and hypotension. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:severe allergic transfusion reaction|actions:stop the transfusion and maintain IV access with saline using new tubing;activate emergency response and administer prescribed epinephrine/airway support as indicated|monitor:airway and oxygenation;blood pressure and perfusion
items.rationale: Wheezing and hypotension indicate a severe allergic reaction. Stop the product, support airway and circulation, and treat urgently.

items.title: Highlight the actions that reduce injury during transfer of a dependent client: assess mobility first;use a mechanical lift when indicated;lock bed and wheelchair brakes;ask the client to pull on the nurse's neck;use adequate staff assistance.
items.content: segments:assess mobility first|use a mechanical lift when indicated|lock bed and wheelchair brakes|ask the client to pull on the nurse's neck|use adequate staff assistance|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Assessment, equipment, locked brakes, and adequate help reduce falls and musculoskeletal injury. Clients should not pull on the nurse's neck.

items.title: Convert 38.5 °C to Fahrenheit using F = (C × 9/5) + 32. Enter to one decimal place.
A client with a subdural hematoma becomes harder to arouse, develops a new unequal pupil, and has a falling GCS. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Activate immediate neurologic/emergency escalation and prepare for urgent intervention.
items.rationale: Worsening consciousness, pupillary asymmetry, and falling GCS indicate expanding intracranial injury or rising pressure.

items.title: A client with chronic kidney disease has weakness, potassium 6.6 mEq/L, and peaked T waves. The client is alert and BP stable. What is the priority nursing plan?
items.content: Initiate urgent cardiac monitoring and notify the provider; prepare prescribed IV calcium for ECG changes, potassium-shifting therapy, and definitive potassium removal. Recheck potassium and ECG.
items.rationale: Hyperkalemia with ECG changes is an emergency even when BP is stable. Calcium stabilizes the myocardium; shifting and removal therapies lower potassium.

items.title: A client is pacing, shouting, and clenching fists. Which approach is best?
items.content: Maintain personal space, use a calm nonthreatening voice, and offer simple choices.
items.rationale: Calm communication, space, and choices can reduce escalation while maintaining safety.

items.title: Which findings should a client with heart failure report to the care team? Select all that apply.
items.content: Rapid weight gain; increasing shortness of breath; new swelling; needing more pillows to sleep.
items.rationale: These findings may indicate worsening fluid overload and should prompt early evaluation.

items.title: Select the 3 findings that may indicate an acute transfusion reaction.
items.content: Fever or chills; flank or back pain; new dyspnea or hypotension.
items.rationale: These can indicate hemolytic, febrile, or allergic transfusion reactions. Stop the transfusion and assess immediately.

items.title: Match each finding with the likely condition.
items.content: rows:unilateral absent breath sounds after trauma;fine bibasilar crackles with edema;diffuse expiratory wheeze|columns:pneumothorax;pulmonary edema;bronchospasm|answers:unilateral absent breath sounds after trauma=pneumothorax;fine bibasilar crackles with edema=pulmonary edema;diffuse expiratory wheeze=bronchospasm
items.rationale: Unilateral absent sounds after trauma suggest pneumothorax; crackles with edema suggest pulmonary edema; expiratory wheeze suggests bronchospasm.
